return.summary: I read the docstrings and declaration heads of all 16 modules, plus the full opening accounts of 7 of them. I opened no proof bodies and did not read the chapters. In these modules every change of a reading itself is handed in: the update and what is sensed (RevisesBy), the listed candidates (Loop), the schedule, the bound N with the late reading lo' (Thinned.lossPool, shapedLossPool), the window [N,K) with hL (windowRead), and each kind's reading in the pool (DrawnShaping). ReadingsPersist says so in its own words: readings are 'carried and filtered, never varied or learned'. ReadInTime lists 'readers who learn' among what it does not state. Three shapes register a difference that was not registered before without the reading changing. (1) ReadOffInTime, general laws: FirstApart, admits_iff_gap_within_margin, selectsAlike_unreached and readableInTime_iff. The loss itself travels through couplings and crosses a margin, so it reaches a fixed selection read off a supplied group. too_late_of_own: read off the continuations of what is lost, the loss is read only after its point of no return. (2) PoolFromCourse.Borne: bear_shaped_shapers and borne_falls are general; shapers_left is a built example. A loss borne by the shapers enters the counts the selection already reads and leaves the lock with no reader of it. Who bears it and at what rate is handed in. (3) ReadingLoop.sensed_alike_iff, general: two worlds come to be told apart at the first step their answers to the formation's own act differ. The Untested witnesses show the cost (explorer_low_once). floor_forgoes and alike_of_kept show that keeping a task can keep the worlds untold apart. This is the one statement found that ties what can come to be registered to what the formation keeps. Losing is stated: readers are not readmitted (stands_not_readmitted, closed_stays_closed); removed readers change nothing (window_removed_unregistered); fixation under copying is a lock (fixed_of_present); a lock outlives a loss it does not read (lock_outlives_loss). return.summary:
I read the declarations, with their docstrings, of all 15 assigned files, plus the opening accounts and key definitions (step, experience, reform, observed, changed, inspected, process). I also read the wall section of the meta-attractor study and the section after it. Proofs were not opened. Some statements in CorrectionReconfiguration, TestingReorganization, FormativeCapacity (after l.260) and EvaluatorGrounding (after l.74) were seen by name only. ACQUIRED-CORRECTION.md was not opened.

Only CorrectionInquiry imports the Becoming package. Every file supplies its mechanism, and its own header says so.

G4 is supported. Several files state exact conditions under which a lacked route, observation, decoder or ground is acquired by the model's own moves:
- reachable_route_is_found: fuel ≥ nodes, and the tree is inhabited.
- acquired_at_reach: holds for every state s and every n, with no premise.
- complete_records_identify_coupling: SoundRows and Complete.
- training_forms_decoder, and every_reachable_faithful_interpretation_is_correct.
- acquired_history_identifies_origin: holds for every condition c and selection r.
- query_cost_threshold: c < 1/8, with built numbers.

Each of these is a law of one supplied model, or a built example. None is a general law over models.

What is registered is sometimes the effect of the thing itself on the going-on:
- the access loss the agent's own practice causes (GoalFormationRevision.experience);
- the outage pattern a shared dependency causes (CommonCauseDiscovery.observation_is_effect).

When it is read is always handed in: a schedule, a menu, a meter, responsiveness, authority. No law was found in which a loss or fall itself triggers the registering. The nearest is GoalRevision's reform gate: the rule changes only if the old credit would not carry the demand from the fund. That is built, and the demand is handed in.

Losses are mostly unconditional within each model, and acquisition is always conditional:
- closed_no_infinite: a closed socket means no infinite run.
- extension_invalidates and change_invalidates_records: every state, no premise.
- no_finite_certificate_of_unrestricted_separation: holds over any certifier.
- absent_current_route_rejects: unconditional.

Some losses are undone in built cases by re-handing in authority or a reference.

The meta-attractor study names as its wall how ends "form and preserve the authority, evidence, transfers and commitments that change what local success selects". It says one more favourable institutional law would not cross it. On the frozen file's criteria, nothing is "already there" in this group. G5's shape holds of every law found, with the nearest exceptions noted above.

return.summary:
In the group read (revision, and the forming of moves, routes and predictions), no general law has a difference come to be registered because of what it does to the going-on without a rule, reading or record handed in.

What is registered is one of three things:
- a lumping that is a coordinate of the configuration (Revision, OpenedCorrection);
- an installed reference list (ContinuingRevision, ReferencePlan);
- a set of samples and an installed program (RouteFormation).

It changes by a move of one process. The move is chosen by a supplied controller or policy (`Revising.choose`: "Its preference for forming the link is supplied") or fed by a supplied record (`RouteFormation.encounter`: "a supplied code's value").

The nearest case to registering from what was not registered is in ContinuingRevision. There the going-on's own act fails at the unregistered address (`fail_step_at`, l190). After revise, probe and install, that address becomes registered (`new_available_choice`, l317, a built family for every n). The general law behind it is `ReferencePlan.revise_registers_failure` (l446), with the rule `propose` handed in. A blind rule leaves some failure unregistered (`frozen_misses`, l460).

The stock ties in as cost and continuation:
- `opens_without_correction`: forming a distinction can use up the last support for using it.
- `repeats_iff`: the cycle repeats without end exactly where the yield is at least nine.
- `no_run_without_return`: with the return cut, no unending run exists.

TurningInTime's three window laws are the one place where the stock's level sets the rule or the share. Which levels are read is handed in (`corrects`, `sets`, `every`).

Losing is general and exact:
- `lost_choice`: any merge of a pair the old relation told apart loses a selection.
- `coarser_opens_nothing`: a reading read off the old one through a map opens nothing.

Gaining is conditional on a supplied difference (`history_gains` and `retained_gains` both need it as a premise). In the Revising model, closing can be undone by rebuilding, given stock.

HeldPossible's rule tower supports G5's "the scheme is fixed": every rule changes only as the one above allows, and along a fixed process the whole possible never grows. But in Revision and ContinuingRevision the reading changes at the same level, by a move of one process, not by a slower reading one level up.

Outside my list, ReferencePlan, Contacts and `Runaway.policy_uses_after_failure` bear on Q3 and Q6.
